theory.intro: When the perimeter is given and one side is unknown, the perimeter becomes an equation. Write it as the sum of all the sides, substitute what you know, then work backwards to the missing length.
facts: The perimeter is the sum of **all** side lengths, so a stated perimeter gives an equation you can solve.
A side that appears twice contributes $2x$ to the sum: a rectangle of length $L$ and width $x$ has $P = 2L + 2x$.
A regular polygon with $n$ equal sides has $P = n \times \text{side}$, so the side length is $P \div n$.
Undo the sum with inverse operations — subtract the known lengths first, then divide if the unknown appears more than once.
Every length must be in the same unit before adding, and the answer is written with a unit.
Check your answer: a single side can never be longer than the whole perimeter.

foundation.question_text: A rectangle has a length of $8.5$ cm and a perimeter of $27$ cm. Find its width, in centimetres.

development.question_text: Rohan is fencing a rectangular paddock. He needs $8.6$ km of fencing in total, and the paddock is $2.9$ km long. How wide is the paddock, in kilometres?

development.solution_text:
$P = 2x + 2x + x + x$
$84 = 6x$
$x = \frac{84}{6}$
$= 14$
The garden bed is $14$ cm wide and $28$ cm long.

mastery.question_text: The length of a rectangle is $5$ cm more than its width, and its perimeter is $46$ cm. Find the width and the length, in centimetres.

A triangle has a perimeter of $48$ cm and two of its sides measure $15$ cm and $19$ cm. Mia writes $x = 48 + 15 + 19 = 82$ cm for the third side. Explain her error and find the correct length of the third side.
mastery.solution_text:
Mia added the perimeter on instead of using it as the total. The perimeter is the distance all the way around, so one side can never be longer than the perimeter.
$P = 15 + 19 + x$
$48 = 34 + x$
$x = 48 - 34$
$= 14 \text{ cm}$
